answer: The paper's ITL formula ITL = α₀/(1 − λ·W/N_D) holds well in BLIS across rates 1–150 req/s for both always-local (AL, MAPE 3.76%, max error 7.24%) and always-disaggregate (AD, MAPE 2.44%, max error 4.70%). All directional predictions are confirmed: AD consistently lowers ITL (by 0–8.5%) and raises TTFT (by 4.4–15.7 ms) relative to AL, and the fitted W_AD/W_AL = 0.863, confirming disaggregation reduces decode-server work by ~14%. The model exhibits a systematic S-shaped residual (2 sign changes) caused by BLIS's roofline latency model having concave step-time scaling with batch size (weight amortization), which the paper's linear T_iter = α + B·δ does not capture. The fit is tightest at moderate rates (30–120 req/s, <2% error) and worst at the extremes (rate=1 and rate=150, ~5–7% error). No saturation was reached (max utilization ~38%), so the near-capacity regime remains untested.
